# Exploratory Data Analysis Report — Social Engine Dataset (Round 1, Phase 1)

## 1. Dataset Overview

- **Users:** 1,500 records, 5 fields (`user_id`, `location`, `language`, `account_created`, `follower_count`). No structural issues found.
- **Posts (raw):** 12,360 records, 8 fields. After removing 360 exact duplicates: **12,000 records** in the cleaned file.

## 2. Data Quality Issues Identified & Resolved

![](data:image/png;base64,)

| Issue | Count (post-dedup) | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missing `platform` | 1,784 | Imputed via per-user mode (100% resolved , every user had ≥1 other post) |
| Missing `text_content` | 1,688 | Flagged (`text_missing`), not fabricated |
| Missing `likes` | 1,814 | Flagged (`likes_missing`) |
| Negative `likes` (impossible value) | 509 | Flagged (`likes_anomalous`), excluded from engagement aggregates |
| Duplicate rows | 360 | Dropped |
| Mixed timestamp formats | all rows | Normalized to ISO 8601 |
| Undecoded HTML entities | 341 | Decoded |

Referential integrity was fully intact every post's `user_id` matched a real user in the `users` table, with zero orphaned records.

## 3. Platform Distribution

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Post volume is nearly even across all five platforms (Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, Reddit, YouTube), each landing between roughly 2,270–2,630 posts. No platform dominates the dataset.

## 4. Engagement by Platform

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Average engagement (likes, shares, comments) is also strikingly flat across platforms average valid likes range only from \~2,450 to \~2,540, shares from \~980 to \~1,040, and comments from \~500 to \~510. This uniformity suggests the dataset was synthetically generated with similar engagement distributions per platform, rather than reflecting real-world platform-specific behavior (where, e.g., Instagram/YouTube would typically show very different like-to-comment ratios than Reddit).

## 5. Posting Volume Over Time

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Posting volume is stable across the observed 12-month window (May 2024 – April 2025), holding steady between \~915 and \~1,040 posts per month with no clear seasonal trend or spike.

## 6. User Language Distribution

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Users are spread fairly evenly across 10 languages (109–169 users each), with Chinese, Japanese, and Hindi slightly ahead and Russian/Arabic slightly behind not a meaningful skew.

## 7. Top Hashtags

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The most frequent hashtags (`#Reviews`, `#Fitness`, `#BestValue`, `#Eco`, `#SpecialOffer`, etc.) each appear 700+ times out of \~10,300 posts with valid text a fixed, recurring tag vocabulary rather than organic freeform tagging.

## 8. Post Text Length

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Word counts are tightly clustered (mean \~17 words, std \~2.3, range 1–20), reinforcing that post content was generated from templates rather than scraped from real users.

## 9. Follower Count vs. Engagement

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Correlations between `follower_count` and every engagement metric (likes, shares, comments) are essentially zero (all between -0.01 and +0.01). Follower count has no predictive relationship with engagement in this dataset.

## 10. Temporal Posting Patterns

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Posting volume is flat across both day-of-week (\~1,675–1,770 posts/day) and hour-of-day (\~310–390 posts/hour) no weekday/weekend split, and no peak posting hours.

## 11. Distributions: Likes & Followers

![](data:image/png;base64,)**![](data:image/png;base64,)**

Both valid likes and follower counts appear roughly uniformly distributed across their ranges, rather than following the long-tail/power-law shape typical of real social platforms (where a small number of posts/accounts dominate engagement).

## 12. Summary of Insights

1. **The dataset's distributions (platform, language, time) are close to uniform** a strong signal this is a synthetically constructed dataset for the challenge, not organically scraped social data.
2. **No platform shows meaningfully different engagement**, so platform is not a strong predictor of engagement in this dataset as cleaned.
3. **Data corruption was concentrated entirely in the** `posts` **table** (missing fields, duplicates, mixed formats, invalid values) while `users` required no cleaning suggesting the corruption was injected at the posts-ingestion stage specifically for this challenge.
4. **All corruption identified was resolvable without fabricating data**: duplicates dropped, timestamps normalized, HTML decoded, platform imputed from user history, and unrecoverable fields (missing text, invalid likes) explicitly flagged for downstream analyses to handle appropriately rather than silently guessed.

*Full methodology, code, and inline justification for every step are in* `data_cleaning_and_eda.ipynb`*.*
